question.text: Consider the triangle $\triangle{ABC}$ shown above. The line segment $\overline{CH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overline{AB}.$ If $ m\angle BAC= 110^\circ,$ calculate $ m\angle HCA.$
question.explanation:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align} m\angle HAC+m\angle BAC&= 180^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle HAC+110^\circ&= 180^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle HAC &= 70^\circ. \end{align}

Note that $\triangle ACH$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align} m\angle{HCA} + m\angle{HAC} + m\angle{AHC} & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{HCA} + 70^\circ + 90^\circ & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{HCA} + 160^\circ & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{HCA} & = 20^\circ. \end{align}

question.text: Given $\triangle{PQR}$ shown above, which of the following diagrams represents the height corresponding to $\overline{PR}?$
question.explanation:
The height (or altitude) corresponding to $\overline{PR}$ is a line segment that

  • runs from the opposite vertex $Q$ to the line $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR},$ and

  • is perpendicular to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR}.$

To draw the height, we proceed as follows:

  • Extend the line segment $\overline{PR}.$
  • Draw the perpendicular from $Q$ to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR}.$
